item.description:
AgentDock 1.2: agents that collide, a second opinion from the other vendor, and how long your agents wait for you.

  • Collision radar: when two agents change the same file within 20 minutes, both dots get a red ring, each agent's row names the file and the other agent, and you get a notification. Two agents busy in one checkout get a quieter note. AgentDock reads which files each agent changes from Claude Code's and Codex's own session files; worktrees count as separate checkouts.
  • Second opinion: on a finished card in the Inbox, "Ask Codex to review" (for Claude Code's work) or "Ask Claude to review" (for the others), or press V. The other agent starts beside it in the same folder, in a new cmux workspace, tmux window, or iTerm, WezTerm, kitty or Terminal tab, with the task, the files that changed and the agent's summary, and is asked not to change anything. Elsewhere the command is copied for you to paste.
  • Waiting on you: how long your agents waited for your answers, how often, the longest wait and how fast you usually answer. In Activity's new card, the medium Activity widget and the share card. It counts from this version on.
  • Welcome back: after you've been away for a while, one panel lists who's waiting for you and for how long, what finished, and files two agents both changed. Click a row to open it. Settings › Inbox sets how long counts as away, or turns it off.
  • Tokens widget: a second widget with today's tokens by hour, split between Claude and Codex, the last 7 days, and today's models.
  • Answered in the agent itself: a question you answer in Claude's own dialog now leaves the pop-up and the Inbox within seconds, even when the command you allowed is still running. Finish notifications and the banner clear themselves once you've seen the agent or it carries on.
  • The pulsing dots of working agents now cost almost no CPU.

AgentDock 1.1.1: Activity by week and month, which models did the work, and your subagents.

  • Day · Week · Month: below the year, switch from one day's replay to a whole week or month. Each day is a row of its 24 hours, shaded by agent work, under an average day; click a day to replay it. ← → move a day, a week or a month at a time, and the year's squares show which week or month you're looking at.
  • Models: which models did the work, ranked by agent hours for the day, week or month, and your favorite of the year in the summary. AgentDock reads each turn's model from Claude Code's and Codex's session files, and fills in the past year once, in the background.
  • Subagents: how many subagents your agents sent off, of which kinds (Explore, Plan, Codex's spawned agents and its approval reviewer…), and which session sent off the most. Just for interest: their time isn't added to your agent hours.
  • Leverage, "That's like…" and the new cards follow the day, week or month on view. Over a week or month, leverage counts only the days AgentDock knew when you were at your Mac.
  • The year grid is now as wide as the window, hover tips appear right beside the square or the pointer, and cards side by side are the same height.
  • Share: the toolbar has the standard share button, and the 30-day and 12-month cards explain their squares (a square a day; agent hours, less to more). The 7-day bars show their hours.

AgentDock 1.1: Activity, a year of your agents' work, and widgets for your desktop.

  • Activity (menu › Activity…): every day of the last 12 months as a square, shaded by agent hours or turns, with your streak and totals. Click a day to replay it: each session is a lane, each turn a bar, with how many agents worked at once and when you were at your Mac. Press Replay to watch the day play out, or ← → to step through days.
  • Leverage: how many hours of agent work you got for each hour at your Mac, and what your agents did while you were away. AgentDock starts noting when you're at your Mac with this version, so leverage starts today.
  • Records and "that's like…": your longest turn, the most agents at once, your busiest day and longest streak, and what the numbers compare to.
  • Share: a card of your last 7 days, 30 days or 12 months, copied or saved as a 1080 × 1080 image. Totals only: no titles, repositories, branches or anything your agents wrote.
  • Widgets: today's agent hours by the hour (small), the last 7 days and today's leverage (medium), or 20 weeks of squares with your records (large). Right-click the desktop › Edit Widgets › AgentDock. Clicking one opens Activity.
  • The past fills in by itself: a minute after launch, AgentDock reads Claude Code's and Codex's own session files once for the year so far (Claude Code keeps 30 days of them). Everything stays on your Mac.
  • In History, a day's heading now has Replay day ↗, which opens that day in Activity.
  • The free trial is now one per Mac, even after deleting AgentDock completely. While a Mac is on its trial, AgentDock sends our server a one-way hash of that Mac's hardware id and when its trial started, so a reinstall picks up the same trial. Nothing else is sent, and nothing at all once you've bought a license. The privacy page has the details.

AgentDock 1.0.1: fixes from testing every terminal with real agents.

  • iTerm: ⌥⌥ messages and Inbox replies are sent again. They were typed into the agent's input but never submitted.
  • kitty: clicking an agent brings its own window forward, not just kitty. Messages with backslashes (a path like C:\temp) arrive exactly as typed.
  • herdr: questions from agents in herdr can be answered from the Inbox again; newer herdr versions wouldn't show a waiting agent's screen. An agent that appeared before herdr recognised it no longer stays without its name and logo.
  • Claude Code in a terminal opened from the Claude app now shows as that terminal instead of "Claude app", so ⌥⌥ can type to it and clicking finds its tab.
  • When an agent has unsent text in its prompt, AgentDock now says to clear it there, instead of always saying "in cmux".

Tested end to end with Claude Code in cmux, tmux, herdr, iTerm, WezTerm, kitty, Terminal and Ghostty.

AgentDock 1.0: now $19, after a 7-day free trial.

  • Try everything for 7 days. After the trial, the status dots and the hover card keep working for free. Answering from the Inbox, ⌥⌥ messages and answering from your iPhone need a license.
  • $19 once (plus tax where it applies), for up to 3 Macs. Buy it from the menu or Settings › License. After paying, your browser brings you straight back to AgentDock with the key filled in.
  • Lost your key? agentdockapp.com/activate finds it again from your email and the card you paid with.
  • Settings › License shows your trial, your license, and frees a Mac when you move to a new one.
  • The iPhone page says when answering is locked, instead of quietly doing nothing.
  • Fixed: two copies of AgentDock running at once (say, a test build) could cut each other off from Claude Code's hook.

Thank you for trying AgentDock early.
